findings.title: Dependency-policy justification missing from the design doc (card has it; design doc does not)
findings.detail: AGENTS.md dependency policy: additions beyond the starting set require 'a one-line justification in the card and its design doc.' The card records the justification (comment line 125: 'org.clojure/test.check 1.1.1 added to test aliases only — justification: this card's generative scope'). The linked design doc (verification-architecture.md, cited in the card frontmatter) never mentions test.check; its Non-goals (line 30) even state 'This design does not choose permanent lint, mutation, or property-testing tools,' mirroring ADR-004's non-decisions. ADR-004's follow-up work explicitly calls for trialing generative-testing tools, so a one-liner recording test.check 1.1.1 as the trialed library for ENG-017I would satisfy the policy and fit the ADR. Related honesty note for that same line: the 'test aliases only' scoping is nominal — org.clojure/test.check 1.1.1 is already on the production classpath as a transitive compile dependency of metosin/malli (verified: `clojure -Spath -M:run` contains test.check-1.1.1.jar; no production :deps entry was added and no src/ namespace requires test.check, so nothing leaks, but the scoping claim adds no isolation that wasn't already absent).

findings.title: Dead `_broken` computation left in the epistemic law test by the kondo-cleanup commit
findings.detail: Lines 147–148: `_broken (assoc-in payload [:data "repository-location" 0 :observation/schema-version] 1)` is computed and never used — commit 77d636a renamed `broken` to `_broken` to silence the kondo unused-binding warning instead of deleting the vestige or wiring it in. The corrupt scenario that actually runs (line 149) only strips :content-hash from the manifest. STYLE.md §'Verification and warnings' ('Warnings are failed contracts') is satisfied mechanically, but a maintainer reading the epistemic law sees a phantom version-1-tamper scenario that does not exist; in a file whose entire purpose is adversarial clarity, the dead binding should be removed (or the scenario used). Verified the new files are otherwise kondo-clean and the repo-wide 67 lint warnings are pre-existing baseline in other test files, not introduced here.

findings.title: Seeds are not actually printed in the green gate output (kaocha swallows them); no harness entry point to re-run a recorded seed
findings.detail: AC: 'All properties green under clojure -M:unit-test with seeds printed'; completion comment: 'every property prints SEED <label> <n>' and completion evidence promises 'Property run output with seeds'. Verified otherwise: `clojure -M:unit-test 2>&1 | grep -c SEED` returns 0, including with `--focus epiphany.law-suite.generative-laws-test` (10 tests, 80 assertions, 0 failures, no SEED lines). Kaocha's default output capture discards passing-test stdout, so the printed seeds (quick, lines 26-34) never reach the gate output; the 'run output with seeds' evidence cannot exist from this gate. Additionally `quick` takes only [label property] — there is no recorded-seed parameter, so 're-run with :seed' requires a REPL or hand-editing the test; no replay artifact is committed. The underlying replay mechanism itself is sound (I reproduced the comment's demonstration: deliberately-failing undeclared-key property, seed 424242, two runs -> byte-identical shrunk counterexample), so this is about observability/evidence, not correctness.

findings.title: Coverage matrix has no category-level teeth, contrary to the card scope
findings.detail: Card scope: 'Machine-readable coverage matrix: required law categories per registered operation; a registered op missing a category fails a completeness test.' Delivered completeness test (lines 200-217) only compares the matrix's KEY SET against operations/registered-write-operations. There is no set of required categories anywhere: deleting :mutation-rejected from :record-checkpoint! (line 189) leaves the suite green, and adding an invented category (e.g. :time-travel) to any op also leaves it green — declared categories are never checked against any actual test. The matrix is data, but its per-category content is unverified prose-shaped data; only whole-op omission turns the suite red (negative fixture at 211-217 covers only that case). The op-level invariant ('adding a persistence op without declaring coverage turns the suite red') IS satisfied; the category-level scope sentence is not.

findings.title: metamorphic-replay property uses (random-uuid) — the global RNG — contradicting the card's PRNG-purity claim and seed-replay invariant
findings.detail: Line 110: the changed-content conflict leg does (assoc record :observation/id (random-uuid)) inside the property body. The completion comment states 'UUIDs derive from test.check's PRNG — never the global RNG — so seeds replay exactly' and the card invariant requires 'A property failure is reproducible from its printed seed'. For this property the generated record replays from the seed but the conflict uuid does not; a failure here is not a pure function of the printed seed (and a collision of random-uuid with the record's :observation/id would produce a spurious, non-replayable failure). Fix is trivial: draw the conflict uuid from the generator tuple or use a fixed conflict uuid as observations_laws.clj:164-166 does.

findings.title: Per-run op coverage of the mutation laws is stochastic, not guaranteed
findings.detail: gen-op-record (generators.clj:180-185) picks the op uniformly per sample and num-tests is 30 (line 24), so each mutation property has ~(6/7)^30 ≈ 1% chance per op of never exercising that op in a green run (~6.6% that at least one of the 7 ops is unsampled per property). The comment's claim 'Mutation laws over ALL 7 registered write ops' is true only in expectation per run; a schema regression on a single op (e.g. checkpoint map made open) escapes any run where that op wasn't sampled. Mitigated in practice because three independent stateless mutation properties re-sample, and the sanity test (lines 42-53) does cover each op deterministically.

findings.title: Dead code: unused :type-as-string mutation and unused _broken binding
findings.detail: generators.clj:197 defines a :type-as-string mutation that no test uses (only :undeclared-key, :uuid-as-string, :version-bump, :drop-envelope-key are exercised). generative_laws_test.clj:147-148 binds _broken (assoc-in ... schema-version 1) that is never used — the corrupt leg actually works by dissoc'ing :content-hash from the manifest. Neither affects correctness, but both are leftover scaffolding in files the card claims are kondo-clean by construction.

result.dodVerdict: Verification table: (1) 'Generated invalid writes rejected statelessly' — MET: mutation-law-undeclared-key/uuid-as-string/drop-envelope-key (generative_laws_test.clj:55-96) assert ExceptionInfo + export-all before/after equality over gen-op-record spanning all 7 registered ops; version-bump asserted as :schema-version-mismatch via operations/validate-version (79-84); sanity test (42-53) proves generators produce schema-valid records, so the mutation laws are non-vacuous. Caveat: per-run op coverage stochastic (finding 4). (2) 'Epistemic outcomes not collapsed' — MET: epistemic-law-outcomes-never-collapse (132-173) pushes generated records through export, then produces :source/unavailable (missing file; backup.clj:130-131), :integrity/corrupt (content-hash removed; backup.clj:96-99), :integrity/unsupported-version (schema-version 99 with correctly recomputed hash; backup.clj:49-56), and a genuinely-empty import returning a counts map; asserts each expected code and pairwise distinctness. Scenarios genuinely cannot collapse — a shared outcome fails distinct?. (3) 'Seeds replay' — MECHANISM VERIFIED, EVIDENCE INCOMPLETE: independently reproduced the comment's demonstration (failing undeclared-key property, seed 424242 x2 -> identical shrunk counterexample, 'identical replay: true'), so the PRNG-pure generator claim holds for the mutation laws; but no runner output is pasted in the comment, no replay artifact is committed, quick has no recorded-seed entry point, and the green gate prints zero SEED lines (kaocha capture) — AC 'with seeds printed' is not observable (finding 1); metamorphic-replay violates PRNG purity via (random-uuid) (finding 3). (4) 'Coverage matrix enforced' — MET at op granularity: completeness test (200-209) compares matrix keys against operations/registered-write-operations and the negative fixture (211-217) proves an undeclared op is caught; NOT met at the category granularity the scope promises — no required-category set exists and removing/inventing a category stays green (finding 2). Acceptance criteria: 'All properties green under clojure -M:unit-test with seeds printed' — green half reproduced exactly (737 tests, 1988 assertions, 0 failures, matching the card); seeds-printed half not observable (finding 1) => PARTIAL. 'Coverage matrix lists every registered operation with satisfied law categories; negative fixture proves teeth' — all 7 ops listed, negative fixture present; teeth are op-level only => MET with caveat. Gates: 737/1988/0 reproduced; deps.edn change is test-aliases-only as claimed; declared matrix categories for review-decision/lineage-candidate idempotency are backed by the fixed-fixture harness (observations_laws.clj:176-184, 243-264), not by this change's generative tests.

findings.title: Version-bump mutation law bypasses the port; the in-memory adapter demonstrably accepts schema-version 99 writes
findings.detail: mutation-law-version-bump-is-unsupported (lines 79-84) is the ONLY version law, and it calls (operations/validate-version op mutated) directly — it never sends the mutated record through the port, unlike the other three mutation laws. That matters because the write path it should be judging is permissive: the envelope schema pins :observation/schema-version as [:int {:min 1}] (src/epiphany/law/observation.clj:35), so version 99 passes Malli, and the in-memory adapter's validate-write! (src/epiphany/infra/adapters/in_memory.clj:50-62) only runs registry/explain — it never calls validate-version. Verified empirically: ((:record-repository-location! port) (assoc record :observation/schema-version 99)) returns nil and the record lands in export-all (count 1). Meanwhile the mongo adapter DOES reject via operations/validate-version (src/epiphany/infra/adapters/mongo.clj:51). So (a) the law would pass against a fully version-permissive adapter — exactly the permissive-adapter case this card exists to catch; (b) the two adapters now observably diverge on version enforcement, and this suite cannot turn red over it. Fix: route the version-bump mutation through the port like the other mutation laws and assert :schema-version-mismatch + statelessness, and/or add validate-version to the in-memory validate-write!.

findings.title: random-uuid used inside a property — global-RNG leak contradicting the card's headline PRNG-purity claim
findings.detail: Line 110: (assoc record :observation/id (random-uuid)) inside metamorphic-replay-idempotent-and-conflict draws from the global RNG, not test.check's PRNG. The card's completion comment explicitly claims 'UUIDs derive from test.check's PRNG — never the global RNG — so seeds replay exactly' and recounts fixing exactly this pattern. The practical blast radius is small (any fresh uuid triggers the :idempotency-conflict branch, and the shrunk counterexample only contains the generator-produced record), but the card's first invariant is 'A property failure is reproducible from its printed seed' and this is a live leak of the exact kind the card says it eliminated. gens/gen-uuid exists and could be threaded in (e.g. generate a [record alt-id] tuple).

findings.title: Coverage matrix completeness only enforces op-key presence — an op missing a law CATEGORY stays green
findings.detail: Card scope: 'Machine-readable coverage matrix: required law categories per registered operation; a registered op missing a category fails a completeness test.' Delivered coverage-matrix-covers-every-registered-op (lines 200-209) only compares (set (keys law-coverage-matrix)) against registered-write-operations. Deleting a category from an op's set — e.g. :idempotent-replay from :record-review-decision! (line 194) — changes no test outcome; the negative fixture (coverage-matrix-has-teeth, lines 211-217) only exercises the missing-OP path. Additionally nothing ties a declared category to an executed law: the matrix asserts :idempotent-replay/:changed-content-first-write-wins for review-decision and lineage-candidate, but those categories are only verified by ENG-017D's fixed fixtures, so a declared-but-never-tested category is undetectable drift. The matrix is data, but the completeness test has no notion of required categories, so the promised per-category teeth are absent.

findings.title: Epistemic 'generative' property is input-invariant: outcomes are constants and distinct? is tautological
findings.detail: epistemic-law-outcomes-never-collapse (lines 132-173) runs 30 generated scenarios, but none of the four outcomes depends on the generated record: unavailable is a fixed nonexistent path, corrupt is (dissoc :content-hash) on the manifest, unsupported is a version-99 bump with a recomputed hash, empty-ok is an empty export. The property would return identical results with num-tests 1 — the generative wrapper adds zero variance. Worse, (distinct? unavailable corrupt unsupported) at line 173 is tautological: the three values are pinned to three different keywords by the = assertions immediately above, so distinct? can never fail. The law still has teeth against outcome collapse in the import path (exact codes are asserted), so this is oversold generativity rather than a hole — but note also that only the missing-content-hash corruption variant is exercised generatively; the hash-mismatch-with-tampered-data variant remains fixture-only (backup_integrity_test.clj:103), despite the card's 'extends ENG-017F fixtures generatively' scope line.

findings.title: Dead delivered code and constant identity fields narrow the claimed generator variance
findings.detail: (1) The :type-as-string mutation (line 197) is defined but consumed by no law — a fifth named mutation that never runs. (2) gen-inst (lines 27-29) and gen-observed-path (lines 37-41) are unused. (3) The shared envelope (lines 46-51) pins :resource-id to a single constant UUID and :observation/observed-at to a fixed inst for every generated record, while the ns docstring claims 'identity/evidence fields vary within their legal alphabets' — resource-id (the field every list-* read filters on) never varies, so no generated scenario can exercise multi-resource variance. None of these turn the suite red today; all are drift bait in a card whose deliverable is adversarial generators.
